title: Longitudinal relations between body dissatisfaction and depressive symptoms in Black adolescents
author: Yan Wang
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8nnhvde

steps.title: Recruit and Screen Participants
steps.instruction: Recruit Black adolescents aged 12-13 years from middle schools who are participating in a random controlled trial on overweight/obesity prevention.

substeps.instruction: Include participants who are healthy weight (5-85th BMI percentile) or overweight/obese (>=85th BMI percentile).
Exclude participants who are not Black, younger than 12 years, older than 13 years at baseline, or underweight (<=5th BMI percentile).

steps.title: Obtain Informed Consent and Assent
steps.instruction: Ensure all parents have signed informed consent and all adolescents have signed informed assent.

steps.title: Collect Data via ACASI
steps.instruction: Collect socio-demographic characteristics, body dissatisfaction, and depressive symptoms data using computerized audio computer-assisted self-interview (ACASI) at three time points: baseline (T1, 7/1/2002-4/16/2004), ~10 months (T2, 12/2/2002-11/4/2005), and ~24 months (T3, 2/3/2004-11/7/2006).

steps.title: Measure Adolescent Characteristics and Symptoms
steps.instruction: Record specific participant metrics and psychological scores.

substeps.instruction: Collect sex, age, race/ethnicity, height, body weight, birthdate, poverty, maternal education, maternal overweight/obesity, and intervention status.
Measure depressive symptoms using the 21-item Beck Depression Inventory (BDI) with a 4-point response scale of severity to calculate a summary score.

Measure body dissatisfaction using a culturally adapted, age- and sex-specific 9-point silhouette scale (modified from Stunkard, Sørensen, & Schulsinger, 1983) where silhouettes range from thinnest (1) to heaviest (9).
Calculate the body dissatisfaction discrepancy score by subtracting the desired body size silhouette rating from the perceived body size silhouette rating.

steps.title: Perform Statistical Analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze the collected data to examine relations between body dissatisfaction and depressive symptoms.

substeps.instruction: Use T-tests for continuous variables and Chi-square tests (or Fisher’s exact test) for categorical variables by weight status.
Calculate Pearson correlation coefficients among body dissatisfaction, depressive symptoms over time, and covariates.
Perform a trend test for changes in body dissatisfaction and depressive symptoms over time.
Apply a Cross-lagged panel model (CLPM) to examine reciprocal relations between body dissatisfaction and depressive symptoms, accounting for stability across time.
